module_title: International Important Days - Foundational Matrix (Major Environmental & Humanitarian Anchors)
introduction: International Days are designated by the United Nations (UN) and other global organizations to raise awareness about critical global issues. At this foundational level, we focus on the five most celebrated international days that are repeatedly tested across all competitive exams.

core_concepts.title: March to June: The Baseline Global Days
core_concepts.description:
- **March 8: International Women's Day** ➡️ Celebrated globally to highlight women's rights, gender equality, and achievements across political, economic, and social spheres.
- **April 22: International Earth Day** ➡️ Focuses on environmental protection, climate action, and global awareness to save our planet.
- **June 5: World Environment Day** ➡️ The United Nations' principal vehicle for encouraging worldwide awareness and action for the protection of the environment (First celebrated in 1974).

core_concepts.title: September to December: Preservation & Rights
core_concepts.description:
- **September 16: World Ozone Day (International Day for the Preservation of the Ozone Layer)** ➡️ Commemorates the designation date of the Montreal Protocol in 1987 to phase out ozone-depleting substances.
- **December 10: Human Rights Day** ➡️ Honors the day the United Nations General Assembly adopted the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) in 1948.

important_entities.name: World Environment Day (June 5)
important_entities.significance: Established by the UN General Assembly on the first day of the Stockholm Conference on the Human Environment in 1972. However, it was first physically observed in 1974 with the static theme 'Only One Earth'.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Examiners love to swap mid-September dates. Keep a strict boundary: September 14 is India's National Hindi Diwas, whereas **September 16** is strictly **World Ozone Day**. Do not let their proximity confuse you in matching columns.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: 8 Women (March) walked on the Earth (April) to save the Environment (June).
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Chronologically anchors the sequence of the three biggest foundational days: March 8 (Women), April 22 (Earth), and June 5 (Environment).

exam_strategy_tips: In one-liner exams (SSC, Banking, State Police), 'World Environment Day' (June 5) and 'International Women's Day' (March 8) are heavily recycled. Ensure these are memorized flawlessly before diving into advanced themes.
